question: If \(xy=a,\) \(xz=b,\) and \(yz=c,\) and none of these quantities is \(0,\) then \(x^2+y^2+z^2\) equals
solution:
Multiplying two of the given products and dividing by the third cancels two variables and leaves a square. Because \(a,b,c\) are nonzero, \(x,y,z\) are also nonzero, so these divisions are valid:
\[
\begin{aligned}
x^2&=\frac{(xy)(xz)}{yz}=\frac{ab}{c},\\
y^2&=\frac{(xy)(yz)}{xz}=\frac{ac}{b},\\
z^2&=\frac{(xz)(yz)}{xy}=\frac{bc}{a}.
\end{aligned}
\]
Now use the nonzero common denominator \(abc\):
\[
\begin{aligned}
x^2+y^2+z^2
&=\frac{ab}{c}+\frac{ac}{b}+\frac{bc}{a}\\
&=\frac{a^2b^2+a^2c^2+b^2c^2}{abc}\\
&=\frac{(ab)^2+(ac)^2+(bc)^2}{abc}.
\end{aligned}
\]
This is choice E.
